explanation_en: This expression is used to assign partial responsibility for a negative outcome. 'Culpa' means blame or fault, and adding 'parte de' softens the accusation to 'part of the blame.' It is followed by the preposition 'de' to indicate what the blame is for.

examples.en_text: The company director also shares the blame for the project not working out.
examples.target_text: El director de la empresa también tiene parte de la culpa de que el proyecto no funcionara.

examples.en_text: I think we are partly to blame for not having talked about this sooner.
examples.target_text: Creo que nosotros tenemos parte de la culpa por no haber hablado de esto antes.

examples.en_text: Don't complain so much; you are also partly to blame for what happened to the car.
examples.target_text: No te quejes tanto; tú también tienes parte de la culpa de lo que pasó con el coche.

examples.en_text: Citizens say that politicians share the blame for the current crisis.
examples.target_text: Los ciudadanos dicen que los políticos tienen parte de la culpa de la crisis actual.

examples.en_text: I know I made a mistake and I admit that I am partly to blame for the misunderstanding.
examples.target_text: Sé que cometí un error y admito que tengo parte de la culpa del malentendido.

examples.en_text: The bad weather is partly to blame for the outdoor concert being canceled.
examples.target_text: El mal tiempo tiene parte de la culpa de que se cancelara el concierto al aire libre.

explanation_en: A highly elegant prepositional locution used instead of the simple verb 'esperando.' It translates to 'waiting for' or 'pending' and is widely used in formal, journalistic, and administrative contexts. It is always followed by a noun or an infinitive verb.

examples.en_text: We are waiting for your response to be able to sign the contract.
examples.target_text: Estamos a la espera de su respuesta para poder firmar el contrato.

examples.en_text: The passengers stayed in the terminal waiting for news about their flight.
examples.target_text: Los pasajeros se quedaron en la terminal a la espera de noticias sobre su vuelo.

examples.en_text: I've been at home all morning waiting for an important package.
examples.target_text: Llevo toda la mañana en casa a la espera de un paquete importante.

examples.en_text: The patient is still in the hospital waiting for the medical results.
examples.target_text: El paciente sigue en el hospital a la espera de los resultados médicos.

examples.en_text: The project is paused waiting for the director's approval.
examples.target_text: El proyecto está pausado a la espera de la aprobación del director.

examples.en_text: Many customers are queuing in front of the store waiting for the new product.
examples.target_text: Muchos clientes hacen cola frente a la tienda a la espera del nuevo producto.

explanation_en: This extremely common idiomatic formula is used to express 'so far' within a specific time period (usually a year, month, or week). The structure is 'en lo que va de' + [time period]. It is a vital phrase for news reporting, statistics, and everyday updates on progress.

examples.en_text: It has rained very little so far this year.
examples.target_text: Ha llovido muy poco en lo que va del año.

examples.en_text: So far this month, sales have gone up by ten percent.
examples.target_text: En lo que va del mes, las ventas han subido un diez por ciento.

examples.en_text: Our team hasn't lost any matches so far in the tournament.
examples.target_text: Nuestro equipo no ha perdido ningún partido en lo que va del torneo.

examples.en_text: I have already received more than twenty emails so far today.
examples.target_text: Ya he recibido más de veinte correos en lo que va del día.

examples.en_text: So far this quarter, we have read three books in literature class.
examples.target_text: En lo que va del trimestre, hemos leído tres libros en la clase de literatura.

examples.en_text: We haven't had any technical problems so far in the project.
examples.target_text: No hemos tenido ningún problema técnico en lo que va del proyecto.

explanation_en: This extremely common idiom means 'to have something to do with' or 'to be related to.' In this specific source phrase, it uses the subjunctive 'tenga' because it follows 'descartó que' (ruled out that), which triggers the subjunctive. The negative form is 'no tener nada que ver con' (to have nothing to do with).

examples.en_text: I don't think this problem has anything to do with the software update.
examples.target_text: No creo que este problema tenga algo que ver con la actualización del software.

examples.en_text: Do you think his bad mood has something to do with tomorrow's exam?
examples.target_text: ¿Crees que su mal humor tiene algo que ver con el examen de mañana?

examples.en_text: The police are investigating if the robbery had something to do with the abandoned car.
examples.target_text: La policía investiga si el robo tenía algo que ver con el coche abandonado.

examples.en_text: It's possible that the flight cancellation has something to do with the pilots' strike.
examples.target_text: Es posible que la cancelación del vuelo tenga algo que ver con la huelga de pilotos.

examples.en_text: She suspects that the change of plans has something to do with her parents' visit.
examples.target_text: Ella sospecha que el cambio de planes tiene algo que ver con la visita de sus padres.

examples.en_text: I wonder if your headache has something to do with the few hours of sleep you got.
examples.target_text: Me pregunto si tu dolor de cabeza tendrá algo que ver con las pocas horas que dormiste.

explanation_en: 'Poner en duda' is a very common idiomatic collocation meaning to express skepticism or uncertainty about something's validity, truth, or future. It is widely used in political, academic, and everyday discussions. It is more active and natural than simply saying 'dudar de.'

examples.en_text: His recent attitude calls into question his commitment to the project.
examples.target_text: Su actitud reciente pone en duda su compromiso con el proyecto.

examples.en_text: The new data cast doubt on the previous theory.
examples.target_text: Los nuevos datos ponen en duda la teoría anterior.

examples.en_text: The witness lied, and that cast doubt on his entire statement.
examples.target_text: El testigo mintió y eso puso en duda toda su declaración.

examples.en_text: Nobody questions that she is the best candidate for the job.
examples.target_text: Nadie pone en duda que ella es la mejor candidata para el puesto.

examples.en_text: I would never call your honesty into question; we've been friends for years.
examples.target_text: Yo nunca pondría en duda tu honestidad, somos amigos desde hace años.

examples.en_text: In this meeting, your professionalism is not being called into question; we are only discussing the budget.
examples.target_text: En esta reunión no se pone en duda tu profesionalidad, solo discutimos el presupuesto.

explanation_en: This is a very common, slightly formal synonym for 'hacer' or 'realizar'. It is widely used in news, projects, and professional settings to describe executing a plan, task, or project. Avoid using it for simple, everyday actions like washing dishes; reserve it for structured activities.

examples.en_text: The team carried out the project with great success.
examples.target_text: El equipo llevó a cabo el proyecto con mucho éxito.

examples.en_text: It is difficult to carry out this plan without a clear budget.
examples.target_text: Es difícil llevar a cabo este plan sin un presupuesto claro.

examples.en_text: The police are carrying out an investigation into the accident.
examples.target_text: La policía está llevando a cabo una investigación sobre el accidente.

examples.en_text: I hope to carry out all of my New Year's resolutions.
examples.target_text: Espero llevar a cabo todos mis propósitos de año nuevo.

examples.en_text: The meeting was held yesterday afternoon in the main office.
examples.target_text: La reunión se llevó a cabo ayer por la tarde en la oficina principal.

examples.en_text: If we don't work together, we won't be able to carry out this highly complex task.
examples.target_text: Si no trabajamos juntos, no podremos llevar a cabo esta tarea tan compleja.

explanation_en: This is a common colloquial expression used by hosts, presenters, or speakers to keep the audience's attention and tell them not to leave or change the channel. It uses the plural formal imperative (ustedes) or can be adapted to 'no te muevas' for singular informal. It's a great natural phrase for transitions.

examples.en_text: We'll be back in two minutes with more music, so don't go anywhere.
examples.target_text: Volvemos en dos minutos con más música, así que no se muevan de ahí.

examples.en_text: I'm going to pay at the register; please, don't move from there.
examples.target_text: Voy a pagar en la caja; por favor, no se muevan de ahí.

examples.en_text: Stay seated, I'll bring you the coffee; don't move from there.
examples.target_text: Quédate sentado, yo te traigo el café; no te muevas de ahí.

examples.en_text: Wait a moment while I check the X-ray, please don't move from there.
examples.target_text: Espere un momento mientras reviso la radiografía, por favor no se mueva de ahí.

examples.en_text: The director is on his way for the group photo, so don't go anywhere.
examples.target_text: El director viene en camino para la foto de grupo, así que no se muevan de ahí.

examples.en_text: We will buy the tickets right now; don't move from there so you don't get lost.
examples.target_text: Compraremos los boletos ahora mismo; no se muevan de ahí para no perderse.

explanation_en: This prepositional phrase is used to indicate the medium or channel through which something is done, as well as physical passage. It is much more common and natural in Spanish than 'por medio de' or 'mediante' in everyday speech. It is a key connector for B2/C1 learners to sound fluent.

examples.en_text: I could see the sunrise through my bedroom window.
examples.target_text: Pude ver el amanecer a través de la ventana de mi habitación.

examples.en_text: We met through a language exchange app.
examples.target_text: Nos conocimos a través de una aplicación de intercambio de idiomas.

examples.en_text: I learned a lot about the local culture through their traditional songs.
examples.target_text: Aprendí mucho sobre la cultura local a través de sus canciones tradicionales.

examples.en_text: The river passes through a beautiful forest before reaching the sea.
examples.target_text: El río pasa a través de un hermoso bosque antes de llegar al mar.

examples.en_text: The director will communicate with the employees through an email.
examples.target_text: El director se comunicará con los empleados a través de un correo electrónico.

examples.en_text: Through the years, our friendship has become stronger and stronger.
examples.target_text: A través de los años, nuestra amistad se ha vuelto cada vez más fuerte.

explanation_en: This is the standard idiomatic way to say 'to contact someone' or 'to get in touch'. While the verb 'contactar' exists, 'ponerse en contacto (con)' sounds much more natural and native. It is widely used in both personal and professional correspondence.

examples.en_text: If you have any questions, you can get in touch with me at any time.
examples.target_text: Si tienes alguna pregunta, puedes ponerte en contacto conmigo en cualquier momento.

examples.en_text: The director got in touch with us to offer us the job.
examples.target_text: El director se puso en contacto con nosotros para ofrecernos el puesto.

examples.en_text: I hope they get in touch with the office before Friday.
examples.target_text: Espero que ellos se pongan en contacto con la oficina antes del viernes.

examples.en_text: Tomorrow I will get in touch with customer service.
examples.target_text: Mañana me pondré en contacto con el servicio de atención al cliente.

examples.en_text: We need to get in touch with the apartment owner as soon as possible.
examples.target_text: Necesitamos ponernos en contacto con el dueño del apartamento lo antes posible.

examples.en_text: Get in touch with them if you decide to come on the trip.
examples.target_text: Ponte en contacto con ellos si decides venir al viaje.

explanation_en: Similar to 'llevar a cabo', this expression means to carry out, execute, or lead a project or initiative. It has a connotation of driving something forward or managing it through to completion. It is very common in professional, political, and community contexts.

examples.en_text: We have to carry out this project despite the difficulties.
examples.target_text: Tenemos que llevar adelante este proyecto a pesar de las dificultades.

examples.en_text: She managed to support and move her family forward all by herself after the crisis.
examples.target_text: Ella sola logró llevar adelante a su familia tras la crisis.

examples.en_text: The government is carrying out a new educational reform this year.
examples.target_text: El gobierno lleva adelante una nueva reforma educativa este año.

examples.en_text: It won't be easy, but we will carry out the plan we agreed on.
examples.target_text: No será fácil, pero llevaremos adelante el plan que acordamos.

examples.en_text: The neighbors carried out a campaign to clean the neighborhood park.
examples.target_text: Los vecinos llevaron adelante una campaña para limpiar el parque del barrio.

examples.en_text: It is difficult to run your own business without financial help.
examples.target_text: Es difícil llevar adelante un negocio propio sin ayuda financiera.

explanation_en: This is one of the most common Spanish idioms for 'to bear in mind' or 'to consider'. It is used constantly in both spoken and written Spanish. A common pitfall is translating literally from English as 'tomar en cuenta', which is also used but 'tener en cuenta' is often preferred in many regions.

examples.en_text: We have to take the budget into account before planning the trip.
examples.target_text: Tenemos que tener en cuenta el presupuesto antes de planificar el viaje.

examples.en_text: Bear in mind that tomorrow is a holiday and the shops will be closed.
examples.target_text: Ten en cuenta que mañana es día festivo y las tiendas estarán cerradas.

examples.en_text: It is important that the director takes the employees' opinions into account.
examples.target_text: Es importante que el director tenga en cuenta las opiniones de los empleados.

examples.en_text: They didn't take the weather into account, and that's why the event was canceled.
examples.target_text: No tuvieron en cuenta el clima y por eso se canceló el evento.

examples.en_text: There are many factors that must be taken into account when looking for a new job.
examples.target_text: Hay muchos factores que se deben tener en cuenta al buscar un nuevo trabajo.

examples.en_text: If I were you, I would bear his advice in mind before making a decision.
examples.target_text: Si yo fuera tú, tendría en cuenta su consejo antes de tomar una decisión.

explanation_en: This idiomatic expression means to take responsibility for something or someone, or to take control of a situation. It can also mean to pay for something (e.g., 'yo me hago cargo de la cuenta'). It is highly versatile and essential for advanced conversational Spanish.

examples.en_text: I will take charge of this project from now on, don't worry.
examples.target_text: Yo me hago cargo de este proyecto a partir de ahora, no te preocupes.

examples.en_text: We took care of all the travel expenses.
examples.target_text: Nosotros nos hicimos cargo de todos los gastos del viaje.

examples.en_text: Who is going to take care of the dogs while we are on vacation?
examples.target_text: ¿Quién se va a hacer cargo de los perros mientras estemos de vacaciones?

examples.en_text: The managers have to take charge of the situation before it gets worse.
examples.target_text: Los gerentes tienen que hacerse cargo de la situación antes de que empeore.

examples.en_text: You have to take responsibility for your own decisions.
examples.target_text: Tienes que hacerte cargo de tus propias decisiones.

examples.en_text: After her father's retirement, she took charge of the family store.
examples.target_text: Después de la jubilación de su padre, ella se hizo cargo de la tienda familiar.
